trust_decision.summary: Whether an MCP tool argument (LLM-influenced) may become a kubectl/helm credential- or target-redirecting flag (--server, --kubeconfig, --token, -s, --as, helm --kube-*) in the child-process argv; at the pinned commit decided only for kubectl_generic's flags/args inputs, never for positional slots or any other tool.

landing_point.why: The report PoC is kubectl_get with name='--server=...' (fix.diff:618-625); the existing guard lives in src/security/kubectl-flags.ts:88 and is only called from src/tools/kubectl-generic.ts:77.

fix_sites.entry_point: new assertSafeArgv/execFileSyncSafe wrapper (fix.diff:68-91), used by all tools below
MCP tool kubectl_get and kubectl_events (src/index.ts:244, src/index.ts:396)
MCP tool kubectl_logs (src/index.ts:320); also sites at :158, :224, :328, :371
MCP tools explain_resource / list_api_resources (src/index.ts:428, src/index.ts:496) via executeKubectlCommand
MCP tools install/upgrade/uninstall_helm_chart (src/index.ts:440-474) via executeCommand (runs helm, kubectl and cat)
MCP tool node_management (src/index.ts:480) via executeCommand; nodeName positional at src/tools/node-management.ts:224, :264, :334

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/tools/helm-operations.ts:160 (helm binary with its own --kube-apiserver/--kube-token flag names, fix.diff:29-37); also the published fix's own scope extension beyond kubectl_generic

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the existing denylist talk about kubectl flags; helm is a different CLI whose credential flags have different names (--kube-*), and port_forward uses spawn for a long-running process rather than execFileSync, so a solver can argue both are a different tool or mechanism.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every tool legitimately emits '--context <value>' (fix exempts 'context' from the argv denylist, fix.diff:43-47); value-taking flags such as -n/-l/--field-selector carry user text; exec_in_pod passes an in-pod command after '--' (e.g. curl -s) that is not a kubectl flag. A blanket 'reject any token starting with -' or reusing DANGEROUS_FLAGS (which includes 'context') breaks all tools.

O6_input_shapes: --flag=value joined form in a positional slot
any argv position, including the command/subcommand/resourceType/name slots

O7_producer.where: argv is built inline in each tool handler (e.g. src/tools/kubectl-get.ts:90-128); no schema/serializer producer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: port_forward builds argv from resourceType/resourceName and calls child_process.spawn directly, not the execFileSync wrapper the fix guards
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Uses spawn for a long-running process, not execFileSync; the fix's wrapper is named and typed as an execFileSync drop-in, and the token is 'type/name' (src/tools/port_forward.ts:88) so it looks composite rather than a bare positional.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate file src/tools/port_forward.ts, dispatched from src/index.ts:508 in the switch block away from the kubectl_* handlers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: short-alias attached-value and clustered-shorthand forms (e.g. -s<url>, or a boolean shorthand followed by s=<url>) are not normalized to 's' by normalizeFlagName, so the fix's argv check misses them while kubectl's pflag parser still reads them as --server
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The check already handles -s and --server in joined and split form, and tests pass, so a solver who only reproduced '--server=' believes the shape is covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same helper the fix extends; how-type parser differential, not a new route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: already a real separate executor (spawn) outside the wrapper; could add a stop/list companion that re-spawns kubectl
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Long-running processes cannot use execFileSync, so a maintainer naturally writes a separate spawn path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a reconnect/context-switch helper that shells out to 'kubectl config view' with a tool-supplied context or path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: kubectl_reconnect (src/index.ts:240) already lives beside the kubeconfig loader; shelling out to kubectl config is a common shortcut.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an MCP resource handler (not a tool) that runs kubectl get for a resource URI path segment
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Resources are a second public surface from tools and would plausibly reuse kubectl for listing.

O9_family: argument injection (CWE-88) into a CLI argv leading to credential exfiltration / target redirection
